observations: A treadle-style manual sewing machine mounted in a wooden cabinet/table, outdoors on a paved area.
Machine head shows the word 'MERCURY' embossed on the front panel (clearly visible in photo 1).
Visible paint flaking, scratches, and rust-colored staining on the machine body (photos 1 and 2).
Wooden cabinet is maroon-painted, has side drawers, and a cast-iron treadle base with a leather/rubber drive belt visible (photo 3).
No motor, power cord, or foot pedal switch visible — appears to be a manual treadle-powered machine, not electric.
No photo shows the machine being operated, threaded, or stitching fabric.
Background shows an outdoor shop/stall setting with advertising banners, consistent with a roadside seller location in Nigeria.

claims.evidence: Photos 1 and 2 show visible paint chipping, surface rust/staining, and worn chrome on the machine body, inconsistent with 'perfect condition'.

risks.risk: Mechanical function (stitching, needle movement, tension, treadle drive) cannot be confirmed from static photos.
risks.proof: A short video clip of the treadle being pedaled and the machine stitching a scrap of fabric.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged internal parts (bobbin case, shuttle, belt condition) not visible in photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the underside/bobbin area and the drive belt.

risks.risk: Cabinet structural integrity (drawers, hinges, treadle legs) only shown from limited angles.
risks.proof: Photos of drawers opened and a close-up of the treadle legs/hinges.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic/furniture-grade only, no functional premium

proof_requests: Video of the machine being treadled and stitching a piece of cloth.
Close-up photo of the bobbin/shuttle area and drive belt.
Photo of any serial plate or model number on the machine head for exact identification.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Mercury-branded manual treadle sewing machine in a wooden cabinet, but visible wear contradicts the 'perfect condition' claim and no functional proof is given, so it must be priced at worst case (not confirmed working) against comparable manual/basic sewing machines.
